issues.description: Return type mismatch for Stock.take(String): The problem statement's UML specifies Stock.take(String) returns int, and the provided solution implements take(...) returning an int (using -1 to indicate failure). However, the template repository's Stock.take(...) returns boolean. This mismatch is structural: students following the specification (or the solution's usage) will expect an int and may write code that checks for -1, but the template's boolean signature will not compile with that usage and will confuse/ block students when they try to implement SealSaloon logic that depends on the int semantics of take().
issues.suggested_fix: Align the template with the specification and solution: change the signature of Stock.take(String) in the template to return int (not boolean) and implement it to return -1 when the ingredient does not exist or quantity < 1, otherwise decrement the quantity and return the new quantity. Update any template comments/tests to reflect the int-based contract so students can implement SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() consistent with the UML/specification.
